proves.claim: file fallback stores a generated board key privately and reads it independently of keyRef.

keys.relay.file-fallback-stores-a-genera.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: fallback refuses missing or wrong board identities, invalid/corrupt keys, and forget removes only that key.

keys.relay.fallback-refuses-missing-or-w.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: PULLBOARD_RELAY_KEY is a canonical device-only fallback when no stored key exists.

keys.relay.pullboard-relay-key-is-a-cano.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: owner-only key file refuses mismatched environment keys without exposing either source.

keys.relay.owner-only-key-file-refuses-m.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: an account root survives storage loss through credential and recovery envelopes.

keys.enrollment.an-account-root-survives.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: device enrollment keeps its private P-256 key non-extractable and authenticates the exact key.

keys.device.device-enrollment-keeps-its-.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: device wraps encrypt a board key to one device and authenticate board, device and engine.

keys.device.device-wraps-encrypt-a-board.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: wrapBoardKeyToRoster given a board key and a roster of three devices returns one envelope per device, keyed by deviceId.

keys.roster.wrapboardkeytoroster-given-a.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: each roster envelope unwraps to the board key only with its own device private key; another roster device key refuses DEVICE_WRAP_AUTH.

keys.roster.each-roster-envelope-unwraps.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: rotateBoardKeyForRoster returns a new 32-byte key with one envelope per remaining device and none for the removed one.

keys.rotation.rotateboardkeyforroster-re.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: every remaining envelope unwraps to the new key with its own private key and the removed device key unwraps none.

keys.rotation.every-remaining-envelope-u.why: Without it this behaviour could regress with no test naming what it proved.

proves.claim: every keys-cell test has a stable ID and one complete record, and an unregistered test is reported and fails only in strict mode.

keys.registry.complete.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: Every test file in packages/keys/tests that reads files carries an input header naming the cells it reads.

keys.inputs.every-test-file-in-packages-.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: With the declared-inputs rule on, no keys-cell reader is reported, and a header names a cell, never the whole tree.

keys.inputs.with-the-declared-inputs-rul.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: clause 1: createSigningAdapter and createFakeSigningAdapter both sign a message and verify it true with the same public key, and false for a changed message.

keys.adapter-signing.both-forms-sign-and.why: Keeps the real and fake signing forms under one contract.

proves.claim: clause 2: both signing forms refuse an empty message with the same named refusal.

keys.adapter-signing.both-forms-refuse-a.why: Keeps the two signing forms refusing alike.

proves.claim: signWith signs ES256 and RS256 tokens over a caller PEM key into base64url signatures node:crypto accepts, and the fake answers the same table with stable strings.

keys.io-adapter-signing.alg-signwith-es2.why: Without it the relay callers keep their own crypto calls outside the adapter boundary.

proves.claim: Both signing forms refuse an unknown algorithm or an unreadable key with the same named refusals SIGN_ALGORITHM and SIGN_KEY.

keys.io-adapter-signing.signwith-refusal.why: Without it the fake accepts keys the real form cannot read, so a test on the fake hides a refusal in production.

proves.claim: Both signing forms with encoding der return base64url keys and signatures and sign and verify under one table.

keys.io-adapter-signing.der-contract-tab.why: Callers that store base64url DER keys could not route through the adapter.

proves.claim: Both factories on the keys front door run the same table and the default PEM form is unchanged.

keys.io-adapter-signing.der-front-door-s.why: A factory missing from the front door or a changed PEM default breaks callers.
